terms.term: Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva (third term), 2023-

posts.post: President of Brazil (acting from 12 May 2016; full from 31 Aug 2016)
posts.appointed_by: Succeeded after Dilma Rousseff's impeachment process (was her vice-president)

case_links.detail: Signed the law ending Petrobras's mandatory minimum 30% / operator role in pre-salt.
Law enabling early renewal of railway concessions; process ran in his term.
Law cutting Jamanxim National Park for Ferrograo (converted from MP 758/2016); signer not confirmed on the page opened. STF upheld the law on 21 May 2026 (ADI 6553).
Signed Decree 9.159 of 25 Sep 2017 (published 26 Sep) revoking the extinction of Renca; the Aug 2017 extinction decree 9.147 is not attributed to a signer on the page opened.
NTS sale to Brookfield group closed in his term.
PPI import-parity pricing adopted under his appointed Petrobras CEO.
Liquigas sale process opened in his term.
Mining royalty reform (MP 789/2017, converted into Lei 13.540/2017).

controversies.what: Accused by Prosecutor-General Rodrigo Janot in 2017 of passive corruption (Rocha Loures / JBS), obstruction of justice and criminal organization ('quadrilhao do PMDB'); the Chamber of Deputies blocked both complaints in 2017. Arrested 21 March 2019 on an order from judge Marcelo Bretas (Operacao Radioatividade, Eletronuclear); TRF-2 revoked the arrest on 25 March 2019; a new arrest order of 9 May was overturned by the STJ about six days later.
controversies.outcome: Acquitted: the 12th Federal Court of the Federal District ended the Eletronuclear corruption/money-laundering case (reported 6 Feb 2022), calling the complaint generic and based only on a plea deal; the 11th Federal Court of Rio de Janeiro acquitted him in the Angra 3 improbity action (reported 27 Nov 2025). Portuguese Wikipedia also reports acquittal on the three 2017 PGR charges (secondary source). Appeal status of the 2025 ruling not reported.

people.name: Wellington Moreira Franco

posts.post: Executive Secretary of the PPI (Programa de Parcerias de Investimentos)
Minister-Chief of the General Secretariat of the Presidency

people.before: Governor of Rio de Janeiro 1987-91; Minister of Civil Aviation under Dilma Rousseff 2015-16; Caixa Economica Federal vice-president earlier.

case_links.detail: Led the investment-partnerships programme under which divestments were prepared; NTS closing (2017) fell after he left the PPI post.
Temer cabinet minister when Lei 13.365/2016 was approved.

controversies.what: Named in Odebrecht plea-deal material (Dec 2016); arrested 21 March 2019 in the Eletronuclear/Angra 3 inquiry; TRF-2 ordered his release on 25 March 2019.
controversies.outcome: Acquitted with Temer and Othon Pinheiro da Silva by the 11th Federal Court of Rio de Janeiro in the Angra 3 improbity action (reported 27 Nov 2025), and included among those acquitted in the Federal District criminal case (reported 6 Feb 2022). Appeal status not reported.

people.name: Henrique Meirelles
people.before: BankBoston 1974-2002 (worldwide president 1996-99; president in Brazil 1997-2002); advised J&F on Banco Original from 2012 through his consultancy and briefly chaired the J&F Investimentos board in 2014.

foreign_ties.detail: Worked at BankBoston 1974-2002 (worldwide president 1996-99); BankBoston merged with Fleet in 1999 to form FleetBoston.

Advised J&F on structuring Banco Original from early 2012; temporarily chaired the J&F Investimentos board in 2014; ended the contract in May 2016 when invited to the Finance Ministry. Page states he never held an executive position at J&F.

case_links.detail: Ran the Treasury during the spending-cap era (EC 95/2016) and tax-expenditure growth.
Head of the economic team when Petrobras's divestment plan started.

people.name: Pedro Parente

posts.appointed_by: Michel Temer government (nominated May 2016, board approved)

people.before: Minister of Planning (briefly) and Chief of Staff under Cardoso; president of Bunge Brasil 2010-2014; vice-president of RBS group.
people.after: Executive president of BRF from about April 2018 (while still at Petrobras); resigned from Petrobras 1 June 2018 after the truckers' strike; board member of M. Dias Branco from 27 Feb 2025.

foreign_ties.counterpart: Bunge Brasil (Brazilian arm of Bunge, global agribusiness)
foreign_ties.detail: President and CEO of Bunge Brasil, 2010-2014.

case_links.detail: CEO during the pricing policy dispute that preceded his resignation after the 2018 truckers strike (page does not name the PPI itself).
CEO when the Southeast gas-pipeline (NTS) and TAG sales were negotiated; a CUT article attributes the sales to his management.
Sale of Liquigas announced under his divestment plan.

people.name: Jose Serra
people.after: Resigned as Foreign Minister on 22 Feb 2017 citing health problems.

foreign_ties.detail: A US consulate cable of December 2009 published by WikiLeaks, as reported by Folha, says he told a Chevron executive that the pre-salt rules would be reversed if he won. His campaign's energy adviser confirmed the PSDB proposal would restore the earlier concession model. The cable is relayed secondhand on the opened page.

controversies.what: Investigated by the STF (Inq 4.428) for alleged caixa 2 (undeclared campaign money) paid by Odebrecht while he was governor of Sao Paulo.
controversies.outcome: On 28 Aug 2018 the STF Second Panel sent the inquiry to the Sao Paulo electoral court (no jurisdiction over the facts) and held facts before Aug 2010 time-barred (limitation period halved for age over 70). No later ruling or charge found on the pages opened.

case_links.detail: Mines and Energy minister responsible for the Renca extinction decree (Sept 2017).

case_links.role: Ministry in charge of CFEM reform
case_links.detail: MME proposed the 2017 mining royalty changes.
Mines and Energy minister when the pre-salt law passed.

people.name: Dyogo Henrique de Oliveira

posts.post: Minister of Planning, Development and Management

people.before: Federal civil servant since 1998 (Finance Ministry); adjunct executive secretary at Fazenda 2011-13; chair of Banco do Nordeste board.

case_links.detail: BNDES financed the TAG/NTS context; he led the bank at the end of 2018.

people.name: Ilan Goldfajn
people.before: Chief economist and partner at Itau Unibanco (2009-2016); IMF economist 1996-99.
people.after: President of Credit Suisse Brasil (Sep 2019-Dec 2021); IMF Western Hemisphere Department director (Sep 2021-Nov 2022); president of the Inter-American Development Bank from 19 Dec 2022.

foreign_ties.detail: Economist at the IMF Oct 1996-Jan 1999; Director of the Western Hemisphere Department Sep 2021-Nov 2022.
President of Credit Suisse Brasil, Sep 2019-Dec 2021.
Elected president 20 Nov 2022; took office 19 Dec 2022.

case_links.detail: Monetary policy during the era; no direct decision on a specific transfer.

people.name: Jair Bolsonaro
people.after: (unverified) Convicted by the STF for the coup plot; conviction final on 25 Nov 2025; in custody (see controversies).

case_links.detail: Eletrobras capitalization law passed in his term.
RLAM sold to Mubadala in his term.
Sent the bill on mining on Indigenous land.
Orcamento secreto (RP9) operated in his term.
Marco temporal law passed by Congress in 2023, after his term; he backed the thesis.
PPI kept; he changed Petrobras CEOs over fuel prices.
EFVM/EFC renewal approved by TCU in his term.
Liquigas sale completed in his term.

controversies.what: Accused of leading an attempted coup d'etat (armed criminal organization, attempted violent abolition of the democratic rule of law, attempted coup, qualified damage, deterioration of listed heritage).
controversies.outcome: Convicted by the STF First Panel on 11 Sep 2025 to 27 years and 3 months; appeals rejected; STF certified the conviction final (transito em julgado) on 25 Nov 2025. Taken into custody on 22 Nov 2025 at the Federal Police in Brasilia after an ankle-monitor tampering incident, a measure not directly tied to the conviction. Current custody status (1 Nov 2026) not verified.

people.name: Paulo Guedes
people.before: Co-founder of BR Investimentos (later Bozano Investimentos; left 2018); PhD University of Chicago 1978; taught at the Universidad de Chile under the military regime.

foreign_ties.counterpart: University of Chicago / Universidad de Chile
foreign_ties.detail: Joined the University of Chicago economics department on a 1974 scholarship, PhD 1978; accepted a full-time teaching post at the Universidad de Chile during the military regime (1980s per a Chilean journalist cited).

Pandora Papers (3 Oct 2021) reported he owns an offshore company in the British Virgin Islands; the Ministry of Economy said it was declared to the Receita Federal before he took office. Company name not confirmed on opened pages.

case_links.detail: Economy ministry drove the Eletrobras capitalization.
Pandemic credit lines and guarantee funds.

controversies.what: Reported by the Pandora Papers (Oct 2021) as owning an offshore company in the British Virgin Islands while minister.
controversies.outcome: PGR archived the preliminary inquiry on 1 Dec 2021: prosecutor Aldo de Campos Costa found no irregularity (assets reported to the competent authorities). He and Campos Neto denied wrongdoing.

controversies.what: Investigated in Operacao Greenfield (pension-fund fraud) over FIPs managed by BR Educacional Gestora, linked to him at the time.
controversies.outcome: TRF-1 closed the investigation against him on 6 Oct 2020 ('no proof of fraud by the minister'), adopting the reasoning of judge Ney Bello after the CVM had archived its own review.

controversies.outcome: No charge against him confirmed on the pages opened; later status of the inquiry not verified.

controversies.what: Named by the Pandora Papers (Oct 2021) as holding an offshore company while Central Bank president.
controversies.outcome: PGR archived the preliminary inquiry on 1 Dec 2021 (no irregularity). The Presidency's Public Ethics Commission pursued separate proceedings: TRF-1 lifted his injunction on 7 Aug 2024 so they could resume, and on 3 Sep 2024 STF Justice Dias Toffoli ended three of those proceedings at his request (jurisdiction/autonomy of the Central Bank); AGU appealed (appeal outcome not verified).

controversies.outcome: On 17 Dec 2020 the TJ-SP environmental chamber formed a majority to overturn the conviction (judgment suspended, resumption expected Feb 2021); final result not verified.

controversies.what: Target of Operacao Akuanduba (PF, May 2021), investigated for suspected advocacia administrativa and favouring illegal logging in the Amazon.
controversies.outcome: On 20 Jul 2021 STF Justice Alexandre de Moraes sent the case to the Federal Court in Altamira (Para) because Salles no longer held ministerial office; later outcome not verified.

people.name: Fernando Haddad

controversies.what: Investigated for alleged caixa 2 in his 2012 Sao Paulo mayoral campaign, based on plea deals from Odebrecht and marketers Joao Santana and Monica Moura.
controversies.outcome: The 10th Federal Court of Sao Paulo archived the police investigation (reported 22 Feb 2024), at the MPF's request, citing lack of evidence beyond the plea deals. A separate state-court caixa 2 case from the same campaign was rejected in 2019 and another case archived in 2021 (per the same article).
